title: New catalog knobs' fail-fast error paths have zero negative-row coverage (missing-key / non-integer / zero / negative)
detail: Three new loader rejection branches ship with only happy-path coverage. These knobs are the user's fun-test iteration surface — a hand-edit typo must fail fast, and a validation regression now passes CI silently. Violates the every-knob-has-rows convention.
recommended_fix: Add bal_rows: interval/sep each missing, zero, negative, decimal; plus radius_tiles == terminal_min_sep_tiles (4) equality — the current 'radius at floor' row uses 3, now strictly below the floor.

title: Surge window-boundary assertions weakened to four identical <=1 checks — no discriminating power remains
evidence:
New (9ab2f02), lines 330-333:
```
testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1) <= 1, "surge must NOT amplify at tick 399, got %d", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1))
testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 400, 1) <= 1, "capped burst: tick 400 got %d (≤ 1 = ceil_cap)", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 400, 1))
testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 599, 1) <= 1, "capped burst: tick 599 got %d (≤ 1 = ceil_cap)", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 599, 1))
testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1) <= 1, "surge must end at tick 600, got %d", tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1))
```
Old (8639d5f): `testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 399, 1) == 1, "surge must NOT be active at tick 399, ...")`, ceiling `<= 2` in-window, and `testing.expectf(t, tick_class_count(&state.flow, 600, 1) == 1, "surge must end at tick 600, ...")`.
detail: In-window ceiling and out-window base are both ≤1 at the 4× pace, so all four checks hold in every phase: a director-level window off-by-one or never-ending window passes. Only the pure-function pin (test_set_piece_active_window, demand_test.odin:117) still covers the predicate.
recommended_fix: Pin exact credit-timed counts at the boundaries — e.g. cumulative spawns by tick 399 and by tick 600, seed-pinned per the [E10] convention already used for the ==46/==200 aggregate pins.

title: W6 delivery-side zero-drop contract relaxed to a ratio; staging and assertion comments disagree on the measured drops
evidence:
Old (8639d5f:1117): `testing.expectf(t, res_drops == 0,
		"%d drops landed on a residential sink drop (delivery-side concentration; the estate's sink drops are sized past the inbound bursts)", res_drops)`. New (1233-1235): `testing.expectf(t, res_drops < uplink_drops,
		"%d drops landed on a residential sink drop vs %d at the shared uplink (delivery-side concentration must never dominate the aggregation shed)", res_drops, uplink_drops)`. Staging comment (line 1138): `measured: 3 sink drops at the 4x pace.)` vs assertion comment (line 1228): `in one tick) make ONE thin (40 u/s) sink shed once across the whole run`.
detail: The weakening is pace-forced and documented, but the strict W6 pin is gone: any delivery-side shedding up to (uplink_drops − 1) now passes, and the two comments contradict each other (3 drops vs 1 drop once).
recommended_fix: Pin a quantified bound (e.g. res_drops <= a small derived constant), or reconcile the 3-vs-1 comments and record the thin-sink shed as an accepted consequence for the user's fun-test round.

title: !s.replay_error guard deleted from test_sla_delivery_accounting instead of re-derived
evidence: Parent 8639f5f (test_sla_delivery_accounting): `record_run(&s, 30, cat)` followed by `testing.expect(t, !s.replay_error, "replay_error latched (a logged command failed)")`. New file (9ab2f02), lines 132-134: `record_run(&s, 90, cat)` followed directly by `testing.expect_value(t, s.flow.sla[0].delivered, u64(3))` — the guard survives only in sibling tests (lines 275 and 337).
detail: Assertion removed, not re-derived; nothing in the pace shift requires dropping it. A rejected fixture draw now surfaces only as confusing downstream count mismatches in this test.
recommended_fix: Restore `testing.expect(t, !s.replay_error, "replay_error latched (a logged command failed)")` after record_run in test_sla_delivery_accounting.
